== .claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md
82:#### Changed Files
86:In a project that is a git repository, every task, the latest and each of the previous tasks, lists the files that changed while it ran, between the two snapshots of the working tree taken as it started and ended, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope)'s task snapshots say. In a project that isn't one, no task shows any of this.
90:The files are those `git diff --name-status` gives between the two snapshots, each one added, modified, deleted, or renamed. Each is a row with its path in the project, a small letter for how it changed, A, M, D, or R, in the colour the git panel gives that change, and, for a renamed file, the path it was renamed from, muted, before an arrow. They are listed in path order, below the task's output, beneath the latest task's output table, and beneath an open previous task's table, headed "Files changed" with how many there are. The list is collapsed to its heading to start with, and expands when the heading is clicked.
91:While a task is still running, it has only its first snapshot, so it shows no list yet. A task whose run changed nothing reads "No files changed", muted. A task with no snapshots, as one from before they were taken or one whose snapshot couldn't be taken, shows no list.
95:The snapshots catch everything that changed while the task ran, including the user's own edits made meanwhile, as in the side editor. Each file is compared with the files the harness's tool calls reported writing or editing, as the referenced spec works them out, from its file tools and its shell commands, a subagent's included. A file the agent reported is shown as changed by the agent, its row plain; any other is shown as changed during the task, its row muted, with a small clock icon and a tooltip saying it changed while the task ran but not through the agent.
99:Clicking a file opens its diff between the two snapshots, the file as it was when the task started against the file as it was when it ended, in the [DiffViewScope](../../../ui/components/diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope), as the git panel opens a file's uncommitted changes.
114:Each reply follows beneath its prompt, against the chat's left edge, at the chat's full width, with no box, laid out as the [AskConversationScope](../ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope)'s answers are: the reply text after the harness's last tool call rendered as markdown in the body's text colour, everything before it summed up in one small muted line that expands into the steps, a status line with a spinner and the latest thing the harness did in that line's place while the task runs, and the error it failed with, "Cancelled", or "No answer." at its end. Beneath the reply, in a git repository, come the files changed while it ran, as every task lists them. Prompts are 16 pixels apart, and a reply starts 8 pixels beneath its prompt.
== .claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/index.md
57:Beneath it, each step stays an item of its own, exactly as any previous task is, with its checkbox, status, Resend, and whatever else a task offers, opening onto its own prompt, table, and changed files. The steps are indented from the parent, joined to it by a thin line in the Chain colour down their left, from the parent's heading to the last step, and each is labelled by what it did, "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up", in that step's mode colour, before its prompt, which leaves out the prompt's first line when it is the parent's. They are listed in the order they ran.
== .claude/reference/ui/components/task-table/index.md
75:- "Wrote files", in the theme's muted grey, when it wrote or edited a file in neither, outside the project's own data in .suspense
76:- "Answered", in Ask's colour, when it wrote or edited no file at all, or only files in .suspense, and gave a final summary, as a question almost always does
== .claude/reference/scope/project-data/index.md
13:Everything the application keeps for a project lives in a `.suspense` directory inside the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope), created as it is needed. Nothing about a project is kept anywhere else, apart from the draft.
17:- `history/`: every task sent, as its hidden anchor's source, named by the second it was sent and the anchor's name, and beside it, once its run is over, a `.json` record of the same name holding the compiled userPrompt the harness received, the system prompt as it received it and the harness it went to, whether it has been marked done by hand for sending to the other mode, each line the harness printed, each message sent to the task while it ran, in its place among those lines, any error, and, in a git repository, the hashes of the two snapshots of the working tree taken as it started and ended, as the task snapshots below say
18:- `snapshot-index`: in a git repository, the private index the task snapshots are built with, as they say
30:The draft, `.suspense-draft.pi`, isn't in `.suspense`: it is the prompt being written, as `piton lsp` is shown it, a document named as if it were in the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../project-locations/index.md#project-locations-scope) says, so the server resolves its imports.
34:Some of it belongs to one machine rather than to the project: the harness report `.suspense/harness.json`, the fluency `.suspense/fluency.md`, printed by this machine's piton, the queue `.suspense/queue/`, the commit notes `.suspense/commit-notes.json`, the conversations left `.suspense/conversations.json`, whose conversations only this machine's harness knows, the snapshot index `.suspense/snapshot-index`, and the draft `.suspense-draft.pi` wherever it is, should it ever be written. Git ignores these, so they are never committed. Everything else, the prompt history, the questions, the divergence reports, and the system prompts, is kept with the project.
36:#### Task Snapshots
38:In a project that is a git repository, every task the harness runs keeps a record of the files that changed while it ran. When the harness actually starts the task, not when it is sent or queued, the project's working tree is snapshotted, and it is snapshotted again when the run is over, however it ends: done, failed, or cancelled. In a project that isn't a git repository, nothing is snapshotted or recorded, and nothing about it is shown anywhere.
39:A snapshot is a git tree, made with git's plumbing alone: `git add -A` and then `git write-tree`, run with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing at a private index, `.suspense/snapshot-index`, so the repository's own index, HEAD, branches, stash, and working tree are never read from or written to. The private index is kept between snapshots, so each one hashes again only the files whose timestamps changed since the last. A snapshot follows `.gitignore`, as git does, so ignored files, `.suspense`'s machine-only data among them, are never in it. No commit, branch, worktree, or stash is ever made, nothing is added to the user's history, and no tool but git is needed.
40:Both trees are pinned so git's garbage collection never deletes them, each under a private ref, `refs/suspense/<task>/before` and `refs/suspense/<task>/after`, `<task>` being the task's hidden anchor's name, and their hashes are kept in the task's history record. A snapshot that can't be taken, as when git fails, is left out rather than stopping the task; a task missing either snapshot shows no changed files.
41:The private index and the refs belong to this machine: `snapshot-index` is ignored by git like the other machine-only data, and the refs are never pushed, since nothing pushes `refs/suspense/`.

content.content:
Reply text is rendered as markdown, with no border around it. What subagents do is left out. If nothing streamed but the harness reports a final result, that result is shown as the reply. A finished run with nothing to show reads "No output."

#### Outcome

##### Description

Once a run is over, its final summary is headed by a row of small tags saying what the run did, so what came of any prompt, a task or a question, can be told at a glance. The final summary is the reply text the run gave after its last tool call, or the final result shown in its place; the tags head the last row of that text. They sit above the row's text, in its Output cell, with a little room beneath them, left to right in the order below, wrapping onto another line if the cell is too narrow. Each is a small label in extra small text, with a little padding either side and slightly rounded cor

##### Tags

Each tag is shown only when it applies, worked out from what the run did, not from what it was asked or what it said:

- "Wrote spec", in Spec's colour, when it wrote or edited a file in the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../../scope/project-locations/index.md#project-locations-scope) says, or under .claude/reference
- "Wrote code", in Code's colour, when it wrote or edited a file in the code location, the project config's codeRoot
- "Wrote files", in the theme's muted grey, when it wrote or edited a file in neither, outside the project's own data in .suspense
- "Answered", in Ask's colour, when it wrote or edited no file at all, or only files in .suspense, and gave a final summary, as a question almost always does
- "No changes", in the theme's muted grey, when it wrote or edited no such file and gave no final summary

So a run shows one or more of the first three, or exactly one of the last two. The spec location is the one the task was sent against, as its compiled prompt records, or for a run that doesn't record one, the project config's root; a project whose config gives no codeRoot has no code location, and nothing counts as code in it.
A file counts as written or edited when the run's tool calls report writing or editing it, with a file tool or a shell command, as the referenced spec works them out, a subagent's included; a file only read never counts. Each colour is its mode's, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it, including any colour chosen in the theme editor. The label is in the colour at full strength, on a faint tint of it, about a sixth of its strength, readable in light and dark mode.

##### Not While Running

5:##### Description
9:##### List
14:##### Who Changed
18:##### Opening

use /lib
from /scope/project-data import ProjectDataScope
from /ui/components/diff-view import DiffViewScope

export shape MessageListChangedFilesShape:
    description:
        In a project that is a git repository, every task, the latest and each
        of the previous tasks, lists the files that changed while it ran,
        between the two snapshots of the working tree taken as it started and
        ended, as the @{ProjectDataScope}'s task snapshots say. In a project
        that isn't one, no task shows any of this.

    list:
        The files are those `git diff --name-status` gives between the two
        snapshots, each one added, modified, deleted, or renamed. Each is a
        row with its path in the project, a small letter for how it changed,
        A, M, D, or R, in the colour the git panel gives that change, and, for
        a renamed file, the path it was renamed from, muted, before an arrow.
        They are listed in path order, below the task's output, beneath the
        latest task's output table, and beneath an open previous task's table,
        headed "Files changed" with how many there are. The list is collapsed
        to its heading to start with, and expands when the heading is clicked.

        While a task is still running, it has only its first snapshot, so it
        shows no list yet. A task whose run changed nothing reads "No files
        changed", muted. A task with no snapshots, as one from before they
        were taken or one whose snapshot couldn't be taken, shows no list.

    whoChanged:
        The snapshots catch everything that changed while the task ran,
        including the user's own edits made meanwhile, as in the side editor.
        Each file is compared with the files the harness's tool calls reported
        writing or editing, as the referenced spec works them out, from its
        file tools and its shell commands, a subagent's included. A file the
        agent reported is shown as changed by the agent, its row plain; any
        other is shown as changed during the task, its row muted, with a small
        clock icon and a tooltip saying it changed while the task ran but not
        through the agent.

content.text:
I've changed the spec so a task's "Files changed" list leaves out everything the app keeps in `.suspense`. The code isn't changed yet. `piton check` found no problems and `piton build` wrote 75 files.

**What changed in the spec**

All of it is in the List part of the message list's Changed Files section (`spec/scope/prompt-mode/message-list/ChangedFiles.pi`):

- **Only the project's own files are listed:** spec, code, and anything else of the project's own, such as a README. I didn't read your request as limiting the list to strictly spec and code files.
- **Left out:** everything inside `.suspense` (history, questions, reports and the rest) and the draft file `.suspense-draft.pi`, wherever it is.
- **The count matches:** the "Files changed" heading's count leaves out the same files as the list.
